text:
incident-bot: Paging: Elevated 5xx rate detected for /v1/generate and /v1/embeddings from us-east-1 — automated threshold (error_rate > 5%) hit. Pager: #incidents.

sre-oncall: acked. pulling graphs. seeing spike ~1738502400. lots of gateway errors and connection resets. oncall running initial checks.

jess: any customer reports yet?

support-agent: one enterprise customer (acme-inc) opened a ticket: intermittent 502s since 12:07 PST. saying timeouts and resets.

sre-oncall: copying initial metrics: 5xx 7.3% on embeddings, median latency up 2x. circuit-green for infra but host-level connection resets on inference-frontends.

luis: checking prefix-kv cluster metrics now — eviction rate spiked, key_checksum_mismatch increased, prefix-cache missrate also climbed. looks like eviction storm around 1738502380.

sam: interesting, I see lots of shorter TCP sessions and RSTs between inference frontends and prefix-kv backends. Could be overloaded KV nodes dropping connections.

carol: rolling logs for prefix-cache:
```
2025-06-05T12:06:43Z prefix-cache[worker-3] ERROR kv_read failed: connection reset by peer
2025-06-05T12:06:44Z prefix-cache[worker-7] WARN eviction_event: 1200 keys evicted in 1m
2025-06-05T12:06:45Z prefix-cache[worker-1] ERROR checksum_mismatch key=prefix:abc123 expected=0x9f1 got=0x00
```

sre-oncall: that checksum_mismatch is worrying — suggests corruption or partial writes. Could explain sudden missstorm and downstream 5xx when frontend expects cached KV.

infra-bot: Deploy activity: No deploys to prefix-cache cluster in last 24h.

luis: heads-up: disk I/O on kv-node-7 is very high, and its network retransmits are elevated. Might be hardware flakiness or a bad kernel driver causing resets.

jess: short-term mitigation idea: route traffic for embeddings/generate away from prefix-cache path (bypass) so we avoid cache misses causing soft failures. We can flip the feature flag KV_PREFIX_BYPASS for the inference proxy route.

sam: agree. if we bypass, we'll increase backend load but avoid checksum-triggered errors. also consider throttling eviction via throttle parameter on the cache.

sre-oncall: rolling a bypass for embeddings route now (will affect ~30% of requests -> increased token compute cost). command: ```./infra toggle-flag --env=prod --flag=KV_PREFIX_BYPASS --service=inference-proxy --value=true --route=/v1/embeddings```

sre-oncall: executing...

infra-bot: flag toggled: KV_PREFIX_BYPASS=true for inference-proxy /v1/embeddings @1738502523 by sre-oncall

sre-oncall: immediate effect: embeddings 5xx rate dropped from 7.3% -> 1.1% within 60s. generate still elevated at ~5.5% (not yet bypassed).

carol: applying bypass for /v1/generate too. command queued.

sre-oncall: toggling /v1/generate now.```

infra-bot: flag toggled: KV_PREFIX_BYPASS=true for inference-proxy /v1/generate @1738502608 by carol

sre-oncall: generate 5xx down to 1.3% in ~90s. overall error rate back under alert threshold.

support-agent: informing affected customers: posting interim note to Acme (CS sync): "we're seeing elevated 5xx due to backend cache instability; we've put a bypass in place and are investigating root cause."

ops-manager: good. start live mitigation checklist: 1) bypass in place 2) identify root cause 3) remediate corrupted nodes or bad kernel 4) restore cache with safe integrity checks 5) rollback bypass once healthy. assign owners.

sre-oncall: assigning: luis to root cause + node remediation, sam to network/connection analysis, jess to customer comms + monitor, carol to rollout plan for safe re-enable.

luis: quick findings: kv-node-7 shows disk soft errors in dmesg, sudden fsync stalls correlate to time of evictions. I'm going to cordon and drain kv-node-7 from the cluster.

sam: I'm seeing elevated retransmits on the NIC (ethtool shows rx_errors on kv-node-7). could be NIC hardware or firmware. suggest draining then reprovision NIC or replace underlying host.

sre-oncall: luis please drain. command: ```kvctl drain --node=kv-node-7 --grace=30s```

luis: running drain...

carol: while we do the drain, let's enable per-route rate-limit fallback to reduce backend pressure: set FallbackPolicy=queue_and_retry with small jitter.

sre-oncall: applied fallback policy to inference-proxy @1738502810

luis: drain completed. kv-node-7 marked 'drained' and removed from rotation. checksum mismatch events stopped on pipeline (observed over next 2m).

infra-bot: host replacement ticket created: #infra-3456 — replacing kv-node-7 due to disk/NIC errors.

sam: network retransmits dropped after removal. connection resets dropped by 98%. we should still run a clean cache rebuild to avoid stale corrupted entries.

carol: plan to re-enable prefix-cache gradually: 1) reprovision replacement node, 2) run integrity-only read pass to validate checksums across shards, 3) enable cache for a small percentage of traffic (canary 5%), 4) ramp up to 25/50/100 while watching 5xx and checksum metrics.

sre-oncall: timeline estimate: replacement ready in ~30m, integrity pass 10m, canary ramp 15m each step.

jess: I'll prepare customer update to close the loop once canary stable. keep support on standby for any ticket spikes.

support-agent: Acme updated: "we've applied a bypass to reduce errors and we're replacing the affected node; we'll provide an ETA for full restoration after validation."

sre-oncall: beginning safe re-enable: enabling prefix-cache canary at 5% for /v1/embeddings only. command: ```./infra rollout-cache --route=/v1/embeddings --percent=5 --mode=canary```

infra-bot: canary started @1738503020 route=/v1/embeddings percent=5 by sre-oncall

sre-oncall: monitoring... no checksum_mismatch or connection resets in the canary window (5m). metrics look stable.

carol: bumping to 25% now.```

infra-bot: canary updated @1738503180 route=/v1/embeddings percent=25 by carol

sre-oncall: 25% stable for 10m. no regression. going to ramp generate route similarly but slower.

luis: replacement node reprovision complete and joined cluster. reindex & integrity pass completed. shard checksums verified.

sam: network team ran NIC firmware update and post-flap validation on reprovisioned host. passing.

sre-oncall: re-enable prefix-cache for /v1/generate at 5% canary. monitoring closely.

infra-bot: canary started @1738503280 route=/v1/generate percent=5 by sre-oncall

sre-oncall: canary for generate is nominal. ramp to 25% -> 50% -> 100% over next 30m if no issues.

jess: drafting post-incident note and postmortem ticket: "prefix-cache node hardware failure caused eviction storm + checksum mismatches -> connection resets -> elevated 5xx for customer-facing routes. mitigation: bypassed cache, drained bad node, replaced host, integrity checks, gradual re-enable."

ops-manager: handoff to daytime SRE: please pick up monitoring and finalize postmortem. action items: attach logs, dmesg, NIC firmware version, timeline, and customer comms.

sre-oncall: handoff: incident stabilized, major mitigation actions done, oncall leaving now — handing to day crew.

carol: final note: estimated customer-impact window: 12:06 - 12:28 PST. total affected requests ~0.9% of traffic with 5xx. major customers contacted.

support-agent: will follow up with any customers who reopen tickets.

incident-bot: Incident auto-logged: incident_id=INC-2025-0612-01 severity=sev2 mitigated_by=bypass+node-replacement started=1738502400 ended=1738503300

sre-oncall: thanks team. creating immediate postmortem draft and linking infra ticket #infra-3456.

ops-manager: good work. we'll convert this into a full postmortem with remediation: add disk & NIC health checks to the prefix-kv autoscaler, add checksum-monitoring alerting earlier, and consider eviction-throttle default change.

carol: I'll own follow-ups. leaving notes in #incidents for final review.

sre-oncall: leaving channel.

support-agent: closing interim comms after final customer confirmation.

jess: thanks all. :heart:
